attempted_claim: Let {Δ°_v},{Δ•_w} be a dual dimer configuration in dimension 2 with bipartite graph G, L = L(φ•_w, φ°_v) ⊂ (C*)^2 = T*F_0 the associated dimer/tropical Lagrangian, and (F_0, ∇) an SYZ fibre equipped with a C*-local system ∇. Let CF•(L,(F_0,∇)) be the Lagrangian intersection Floer complex and C•(G,∇) the 2-term Kasteleyn complex of Hicks Definition 3.2.1 with differential d_∇ weighted by ∇. The intersection points L ∩ F_0 are in bijection with the vertices of G, giving a fixed isomorphism of vector spaces CF•(L,F_0) → C•(G,∇). Is this isomorphism a chain homomorphism — i.e. does the Floer differential μ^1 equal the Kasteleyn differential d_∇ — so that the Floer-theoretic support of L equals the zero locus of the dimer partition function Z_G(∇) = det(d_∇)? This is the exact finite statement over C as posed; the Novikov-weighted version with area weights T^{w_e} of Remark 3.2.4 is a separate conditional extension and is not asserted here as equivalent.
decisive_failure: No proof or disproof of the dimer-Floer support formula was obtained. The blockers are structural: iterated extended-region surgery strip analysis is missing and the literal Kasteleyn differential omits sign, spin, grading, and Novikov data. The sign-dependence observation is a gap identification only, not a proved corrected theorem, and is therefore not claimed.
